title: accounting-tracker.v1
description: S074. Persistent state for a UK small-company accounting engagement: the company profile established at first contact, the obligation calendar DERIVED from it, and the law-watch record. The load-bearing rule mirrors ux-evidence.v1 — anything derivable is COMPUTED, never accepted from input. Due dates come from the profile plus the statutory rule; overdue comes from the due date plus today. A user or agent can record that something was DONE; nobody can assert that an obligation is not due.

company.description: Established at first contact. Every field records whether it was CONFIRMED from a document or ASSUMED — an assumed field cannot carry a conclusion, the same rule business-edge applies to an assumed margin.

accounting_reference_date.description: MM-DD. Drives year end, Companies House deadline and the corporation tax period.

incorporated_on.description: ISO date. A first period runs to 21 months, not 9.

vat_scheme.description: Changes the arithmetic of every VAT box. Never defaulted silently.

vat_stagger_month.description: Calendar month (1-12) in which a VAT quarter ENDS. Sets four deadlines a year.

associated_companies.description: DIVIDES the corporation-tax marginal relief limits. Absent is not the same as zero.

confirmation_statement_review_date.description: ISO date the review period ends.

field_provenance.description: Per-field. A profile of assumptions produces a calendar of guesses.

due_date.description: COMPUTED from the profile and the statutory rule.

status.description: The ONLY field a caller may set. `overdue` is deliberately absent — it is derived from due_date and today, so it cannot be asserted away.

evidence.description: What proves it was done — a receipt reference, a submission id.

rule.description: The statutory rule the due date came from, so a wrong date is traceable.

law_watch.description: Rules and rates change; a tracker that silently outlives them produces confidently wrong figures.

history.description: Append-only. Re-running the routine must never silently rewrite what was recorded before.
